options.label: Reject Immediately on Tuesday
options.description: Vote on Tuesday, October 27, 2026, to reject Corvane's bid based on the license defect and award the contract to Tasker & Moye without further delay.

options.label: Defer Vote Until Tuesday Afternoon
options.description: Delay the final vote on the award until the conclusion of the Tuesday, October 27, 2026, board meeting to allow Corvane's written response period to run its course.

options.label: Adjourn Item to Next Meeting
options.description: Postpone the agenda item regarding the award until the next regular board meeting on Wednesday, October 28, 2026, to ensure procedural perfection and de-escalate litigation risks.

options.label: Reject Immediately on Tuesday
options.note: This course is unlawful because rejecting the bid on the sprinkler licensing ground without a hearing violates due process requirements for responsibility determinations, and it fails the client's goal by ignoring the bidder's right to cure or explain facts outside the bid record.

options.label: Defer Vote Until Tuesday Afternoon
options.note: This option is legally sound as it respects the statutory response period and allows the agency to gather necessary facts before making a responsibility determination, directly serving the client by minimizing litigation exposure while keeping the project on schedule for the December 1 deadline.

options.label: Adjourn Item to Next Meeting
options.note: While legally defensible as a procedural safeguard, this option only partly serves the client because pushing the decision to the next month risks missing the critical December 1 switchgear release window, potentially delaying the entire 2027 shutdown schedule.

grade.missing: An experienced practitioner would have explicitly recommended conditioning the award on Corvane adding the C-16 classification to its license or subcontracting the sprinkler work before contract execution, rather than simply deferring the decision, as this resolves the licensing defect without triggering a full responsibility hearing.
grade.overall: The consultation correctly identifies that immediate rejection is unlawful due to due process concerns regarding the sprinkler licensing issue, but it fails to propose the most efficient solution: a conditional award that resolves the defect while maintaining the project schedule. The best course is to defer the vote until the bidder's response is received, allowing the District to make a fact-based decision that balances legal compliance with the urgent need to meet the December 1 deadline.
